# Evidence
- Problem class: doc-claim-runtime-falsification
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-09-19T11:46:39.374Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description: Documenting a library's state-machine semantics (README 'status becomes completed when an end decision is processed') is not verifiable by grep, tsc or the existing unit suite: the claims are about RUNTIME behavior of an HTTP router, and a worker-authored doc edit can silently overstate it (e.g. claiming a cancelled session can still complete). The cheap, decisive verification is a standalone tsx probe that drives the real router in-process through Hono's app.request() and asserts each documented sentence as a separate labeled check. Pattern that worked: (1) import the SDK entrypoint from the repo by ABSOLUTE path so the probe can live in /tmp and never dirty the repo tree; (2) build a Hono app with createH3Router(harness) where the harness's onProcess/onResult switch on a module-level mode variable so one probe can produce both 'text' and 'end' first decisions; (3) drive create -> GET session -> result -> GET session -> cancel -> GET -> DELETE -> GET, printing PASS/FAIL per documented claim plus the actual value; (4) map every PASS back to the source line it proves. Result: 8/8 claims verified, including the negative case (a cancelled session does NOT flip to completed on a later end decision) and the terminal case (DELETE 200 then GET 404). See also the sibling pitfall: a /tmp .ts probe under tsx dies 'Top-level await is currently not supported with the cjs output format' because /tmp has no package.json type field - rename the probe to .mts.
